plan.missing_reason: The SLA does not name an Enterprise plan; the selected plan is not distinguished in the source.

uptime_commitment_pct.quote: GitHub commits to maintain at least 99.9% Uptime for the applicable GitHub service.

measurement_period.quote: “Applicable Period” means the calendar quarter in which a Service Credit is owed.

timezone.missing_reason: The source does not state a time zone for measuring the period.

value.description: Downtime is a period where either (i) the error rate exceeds 5% in a given minute for a Service feature or (ii) the Service was unavailable as determined by a combination of GitHub's internal and external monitoring systems. Excludes Scheduled Downtime and the Section 4 limitations and exclusions.

downtime_definition.quote: “Downtime” is a period of time where either (i) the error rate exceeds five percent (5%) in a given minute for a Service feature or (ii) the Service was unavailable as determined by a combination of GitHub’s internal and external monitoring systems.
downtime_definition.section: 5. Services Covered by SLA, B. GitHub Enterprise Cloud

credit_basis.quote: “Applicable Service Fees” means the total fees paid by Customer for a Service that are applied to the Applicable Period in which a Service Credit is owed.

credit_cap.quote: Service Credits cannot be exchanged into cash, and are limited to a maximum of ninety (90) days of paid service per calendar quarter.
credit_cap.missing_reason: The cap is expressed as 90 days of paid service per calendar quarter, not as a percentage of fees, so it cannot be expressed as a percentage cap.

min_credit.missing_reason: The SLA contains no minimum credit amount.

value.description: Scheduled Downtime for network, hardware, or Service maintenance or upgrades, with at least five days' notice unless a bona fide emergency prevents it
Factors outside reasonable control, including natural disaster, war, terrorism, riots, government action, or network/device failure external to GitHub's data centers
Preview services, or purchases made with a subscription credit
Services, hardware, or software not provided by GitHub, including inadequate bandwidth or third-party software or services
Customer's unauthorized action or lack of required action
Unauthorized access to the network using the customer's credentials or equipment, or failure to follow appropriate security practices
Customer's violation of applicable Acceptable Use Policies or the Agreement
Use of the Service inconsistent with its features and functionality or published guidance
Faulty input, instructions, or arguments, such as requests for files that do not exist
GitHub's throttling of suspected abusive behavior or hacked accounts
Rate limits, performance degradation, or latency issues without actual unavailability, except services with an explicit performance-based Service Level
Use of a Service after GitHub advised modifying use, where the customer did not modify it

exclusions.quote: Downtime does not include Scheduled Downtime, and Downtime does not include unavailability of a Service due to limitations or exclusions identified in Section 4 (“Limitations and Exclusions”). […] A. Due to factors outside our reasonable control […] B. For a Preview, or a purchase made with a subscription credit; […] C. That result from the use of services, hardware, or software not provided by us […] D. That result from your unauthorized action, or from your lack of action when required to act; […] E. That result from anyone gaining access to our network by unauthorized use of your credentials or equipment […] F. That result from your violation of applicable Acceptable Use Policies or your Agreement; […] G. That result from your use of the Service in a manner inconsistent with the features and functionality of the Service […] H. That result from faulty input, instructions, or arguments […] I. That result from our throttling of suspected abusive behavior or hacked accounts; […] J. That result from rate limits, performance degradation, or other latency issues without actual service unavailability […] K. Caused by your use of a Service after we advised you to modify your use of the Service, if you did not modify your use as advised.

prerequisites.quote: Customer must have paid all outstanding invoices to receive Service Credits.

claim_window.quote: Customer may redeem Service Credits only upon written request within thirty (30) days of the end of the Applicable Period.

value.channel: Written request to GitHub Support if purchased directly from GitHub, or through a Microsoft support ticket if purchased through Microsoft

claim_procedure.quote: Written requests for Service Credits should be sent either (a) to GitHub Support if Customer purchases directly from GitHub, or (b) through a Microsoft support ticket if Customer purchases SLA-covered Services through Microsoft.

remedy_form.quote: Service Credits may be in the form of a refund or a credit to Customer’s account.
